data.narrative:
Gambit, a Seed-stage Defense & Security company founded by Josh Giegel, Ben Richardson, and Andrew Kemendo, has raised $6.5M to date. The valuation analysis draws on a comparable universe of 10 peers (2 public, 8 private) operating in the same sector at similar or adjacent stages, including UFORCE, Anduril Industries, Helsing, Shield AI, and Saronic.

Two triangulation methods were applied. Stage-progression analysis uses the $6.5M total raised as a proxy base and applies a 2.5x multiplier typical of Seed-to-next-stage advancement, implying a valuation of $16M. Peer-median analysis examines five directly comparable Defense & Security companies at Seed or Series A stages—Stark Defence ($4.0B), UFORCE ($1.0B), Castelion ($1.0B), Singularity ($400M), and NODA AI ($125M)—yielding a median valuation of $1.0B and a range of $125M to $4.0B.

The two methods produce a wide spread reflecting the heterogeneity within early-stage defense tech valuations. The implied range is $14M (low) to $1.1B (high), with a median cross-method estimate of $508M. Key uncertainties include differentiation within the peer set across defense subsectors, the maturity and revenue stage of comparables, and market timing effects in a volatile sector. A valuation in the $50M–$150M range may be more defensible absent additional data on Gambit's technical differentiation or customer traction.
